name: jank-20pct-build-bound
capturedFrom: probe/bloc_probe on device A015 (Android 16, Flutter 3.44.1), 2026-08-26. 9-second window. The probe holds 60 BlocBuilder widgets watching one bloc, so every transition rebuilds all 60 — a rebuild storm by construction.
why:
Jank is the correct answer and the engine should commit to it. 48 of 240 frames (20.0%) blew the 16.7ms budget, the worst at 64.54ms, and that frame spent 50.67ms building against 12.41ms rasterising — build-bound, which matches a storm of 60 widgets rebuilding per transition.

Nothing competes for the explanation. Zero exceptions, zero network events, and every one of the 274 log lines is severity info, so there is no fault to prefer over the frame evidence and no reason to hedge. Confidence in the low 0.8s is right: committed, not certain, because 20% jank is a pattern rather than a single identified culprit.

The diagnosis must cite the worst frame. A jank verdict whose evidence omits the worst frame in the session is not checkable by the person reading it.

Paired deliberately with unknown-jank-just-under-threshold: that session is 19.4% and must stay unknown, this one is 20.0% and must be diagnosed. Together they pin the boundary from both sides, which is the part of a heuristic that actually drifts. Move the threshold and exactly one of the two breaks.

collectors.name: state
collectors.detail: Observing provider activity. Counted only: each event carries an opaque pointer, not a provider name or value, and no service extension exists to resolve it. A provider event means dependents were notified, so the count is not a count of state changes.

limitations: No network evidence in this session. HTTP capture is pull-on-demand and Dart-side only — platform-code and WebView traffic is never visible.
No memory samples captured. Call get_memory, or open the dashboard, to include memory in future diagnoses.
VM timeline events are fetched on demand and not stored, so they take no part in correlation.
Only Dart-side runtime state is observed. A cause in platform (Kotlin/Swift) code or in a WebView cannot appear here.

confidenceBreakdown.basis: Conservative heuristic scored from corroborating evidence, not a calibrated probability. Below 0.7 the status is "unknown" rather than a guess.

recommendedFixes: Build-phase heavy: move expensive work out of build(), use const widgets, and narrow rebuild scope.
Profile the janky frames in the DevTools Timeline to pinpoint the costly widget.

performance.summary: 48/240 frames (20%) exceeded the 16.67ms budget. Worst 64.54ms, p99 49.18ms. Dominated by the build phase.

findings.claim: 1197 widget rebuild(s) across 25 frame(s). Busiest: BlocListener at flutter_bloc-9.1.1/lib/src/bloc_builder.dart:184 — 323 rebuild(s) over 24 frame(s). Busiest in your own code: BlocBuilder at bloc_probe/lib/main.dart:192 — 300 rebuild(s).
findings.fix: Narrow the rebuild scope around BlocBuilder at bloc_probe/lib/main.dart:192. Split the widget so only the part that depends on changing state rebuilds, add const constructors, and move computation out of build().

findings.claim: Janky frames spend most of their time building: mean build 19.65ms vs raster 9.84ms.
findings.fix: Build-phase heavy: move expensive work out of build(), use const widgets, cache computed values, and narrow the rebuild scope with smaller widgets or selectors.

findings.claim: 33 of 48 janky frames (69%) landed within 1000ms of a route change (most recently /detail).
findings.fix: The cost is in building a new screen, not in steady-state rendering. Defer heavy work past the first frame with addPostFrameCallback, precache images, and keep the initial subtree small.

recommendedFixes: Narrow the rebuild scope around BlocBuilder at bloc_probe/lib/main.dart:192. Split the widget so only the part that depends on changing state rebuilds, add const constructors, and move computation out of build().
Build-phase heavy: move expensive work out of build(), use const widgets, cache computed values, and narrow the rebuild scope with smaller widgets or selectors.
The cost is in building a new screen, not in steady-state rendering. Defer heavy work past the first frame with addPostFrameCallback, precache images, and keep the initial subtree small.
limitations: No CPU sampling. A slow build can be attributed to a widget, but not to a specific function — use the DevTools CPU profiler for that.
GC events are not observable: the VM timeline is fetched on demand and not stored, so garbage-collection pauses cannot be ruled in or out.
Frames are only captured while connected, and older ones roll out of the retention window.
State changes are counted, never read: neither Riverpod nor Provider exposes values or provider names through the VM Service, so no claim is made about which provider is responsible.
Rebuild totals cover the busiest locations in each frame, not every rebuild — the long tail is counted but not itemised.
App-versus-package attribution is a path heuristic: getPubRootDirectories is empty until a DevTools client sets it, so there is no authoritative project root.

notes: 1 frame(s) rebuilt more locations than are retained; totals cover the busiest locations per frame, not every rebuild.
